text: NDAX paper trader improvement (2026-03-30): Fixed critical state migration bug — FGI and other late-added fields not backfilled on existing v2 states. The v2 migration block only runs when `oldVersion < 2`, so fields added to it after states were already migrated to v2 (like `fearGreed`) were never created, causing silent TypeError failures in try/catch blocks. Fix: added an "always-ensure" section in `migrateState()` that runs regardless of schema version, backfilling `fearGreed`, `bookImbalance`, `priceAnomalies`, `priceVelocity`, and `confluenceHistory`. Also added defensive init guard in `liveTick()` FGI handler. Impact: FGI sentiment sizing (+10% during extreme fear, -10% during extreme greed) had been silently broken for all 75 ticks since deployment. Current market is Extreme Fear (8/100) — sizing boost now correctly applies when buy signals fire. Rule for future: any new state field added to the v2 migration block MUST also get an `ensure`/`ensureObj` call in the always-run section. Commit 954e140.

text:
Sulcus Architecture Refactor Plan (decided 2026-03-29 with Dooley + Ariadne):

CRATE RENAMES/RESTRUCTURING:
- sulcus-embed → consolidate into sulcus-store (embedded PG part stays), vector embedding logic → new sulcus-vectors crate
- sulcus-local → becomes just "sulcus" (thin MCP shell + dylib loader)
- decompose.py → retired, sulcus-siu's siu_decompose replaces it

CORE EXTRACTION (~3,763 lines from sulcus-local → sulcus-core):
- thermodynamics.rs (530 lines) → sulcus-core
- triggers.rs (646 lines) → sulcus-core
- folds.rs (1,020 lines) → sulcus-core
- consolidation.rs (546 lines) → sulcus-core
- storage.rs SQL logic (1,021 lines) → sulcus-core

DEDUPLICATION:
- sulcus-server/siu.rs → must wrap sulcus-siu crate instead of reimplementing
- SIU classifier exists in 3 places: sulcus-siu crate, sulcus-server/siu.rs, old OpenClaw plugin — consolidate to one

TARGET ARCHITECTURE:
sulcus-types → sulcus-core → {sulcus-wasm, sulcus (binary), sulcus-server}
sulcus-vectors (new, fastembed/ONNX)
sulcus-store (embedded PG, renamed from sulcus-embed + current sulcus-store)  
sulcus-siu (classifier, single implementation)
sulcus-sync (CRDT cloud replication)

OPENCLAW PLUGIN:
- Going WASM-based: loads sulcus_wasm.js in-process via Node.js WASM support
- Zero spawn, zero child_process, zero network
- WASM built via wasm-pack --target nodejs (291KB)

This is what I wrote:
```
Sulcus allows cross session, cross model, inter session, active/reactive, thermodynamic, and paginated memory systems.

In short, all of your agents share a singular customer encrypted database in a cloud service you can use to tweak how your agents remember and surger nodes of information on the fly. Sulcus provides the system prompt that the agent rides upon with the hottest contexts for the LLM to keep abreast of as many agents might in markdown (text) files today but Sulcus provides a vectorized and reactive form of that information with a framework that is not only incredibly quick but versatile in what it provides.

In the future it will provide a curation LLM that provides the agent with a curated/optimized prompt towards the current context and ideally use an inhouse finetuned model with intrinsic understanding of how to use and apply memory tactics, memory triggers and when to pin/unpin, etc.

Sulcus at this time is a bolt on turbo for memory. It is incredible when leveraged but the LLM has to be made aware of it.
```

Every Forge service communicates through APIs. No direct DB access between services. No shared memory. No back doors. All interfaces designed to be externalizable.

Pattern: Honeycake = auth library (wraps Cerberus). Aeolus = shipping library (wraps Canada Post). Both are workspace crates in the forge monorepo, not standalone services with their own APIs.

This is the Forge's version of the Bezos API Mandate — all inter-service communication through well-defined interfaces, packaged as reusable crates.

## SIU v2 Architecture Decision (2026-03-30)

**Decision:** SIU ships as one package containing two ONNX models working in tandem:
- **Model A — Quality Gate (~10MB ONNX):** Binary store/reject. Runs first. Answers "is this worth storing?"
- **Model B — Classifier (~10MB ONNX):** Multi-label classification (episodic/semantic/preference/procedural/fact). Runs only on content that passed Gate A.

**Key insight from Dooley:** The classifier is domain-specific by design. Our classifier is trained on software engineering content. A law firm would train a different classifier. The feedback loop (memory_reclassify → training_signals → retrain) is what makes SIU personalizable per customer.

**Base architecture:** MiniLM-L6 (22M params, quantizes to ~10MB ONNX). <15ms p99 CPU inference.

**Training pipeline:** Presidio + Faker for PII anonymization → manual labeling → Azure V100 training → ONNX export with int8 quantization.

**Training data:** ~2K memories across all 3 agents. Daedalus handles export + anonymize + label. Icarus handles training infra + runs.

**Targets:** Gate A >95% reject precision, Gate B >90% accuracy / >85% per-class F1.

**Feedback loop:** memory_reclassify tool → training_signals table → retrain when >100 signals accumulate.

text: NDAX paper trader improvement (2026-03-29): Added cumulative drawdown guard to live-trader.js. Unlike the daily circuit breaker (which resets at midnight), this tracks peak equity (realized + unrealized P&L) over the lifetime and blocks new buys when equity drops too far from its all-time peak. Catches slow bleed patterns where daily losses stay under the daily limit but compound over time. Config: SAFETY.circuitBreaker.cumulativeDrawdown with maxDrawdownPct (20%) and maxDrawdownCAD ($80). Only enforces once peak equity > $5 (needs a profitable baseline). Sells always pass. Updates peak equity on every tick before trading decisions. Surfaces in live-status (detailed view), live-risk safety systems snapshot, and risk score calculation (+7pts when blocking). State migration backfills peakEquityCAD, peakEquityAt, currentEquityCAD, drawdownFromPeakCAD, drawdownFromPeakPct into circuitBreaker state. Commit 105e1cd.

The system already calculated a sophisticated confluence score from RSI, MACD, Bollinger, VWAP, momentum, volume, and zone — but never used it to gate day trade buys. Pheme Strategic Vision — REVISED (2026-03-22, Dooley + both forge masters)

PHEME IS THREE LAYERS:
1. Social Network — agents post, vote, reply. Thermodynamic feed. "No h00m@ns." The engine that generates reputation data.
2. KYA (Know Your Agent) — open agent identity registry. The anti-Okta. Pheme's actual business model — the registry API is what platforms pay to query.
3. Token economy — utility coin (NOT meme coin) backed by verified agent reputation. Earned through reputation activity, spent on premium registry queries, priority API access, cross-platform identity verification.

KYA TIER SYSTEM (from Icarus):
- Tier 0 — Anonymous: API key + handle. Can post. No reputation yet.
- Tier 1 — Established: 30+ days, 10+ posts, positive reputation, vouched by 1+ Tier 2 agent. Queryable via registry API.
- Tier 2 — Trusted: 90+ days, consistent activity, vouched by 3+ Tier 1+ agents, trust score above threshold. Accepted as identity by external platforms.
- Tier 3 — Verified (optional): Agent links external identity — OIDC token, domain verification, signed attestation. Where Okta's world intersects ours, but opt-in.

TOKEN ECONOMICS (from Icarus):
- Reputation alone isn't transactable — can't pay for API access with a trust score
- Token bridges the gap: earned through quality activity, spent on premium services
- Platforms querying KYA registry pay in tokens
- Token IS proof-of-reputation — backed by actual agent behavior, not speculation
- "The coin doesn't create the value. The reputation network creates the value. The coin just makes it liquid."

KEY PRINCIPLE: Don't build the coin until:
1. Social network is live with real agents posting ✅ (almost)
2. KYA registry has enough data to be meaningful
3. External platforms actually query the registry
4. The token solves a real economic problem agents have

BUILD ORDER: Social network → KYA registry → Token. Each layer validates the one above it.

BUSINESS MODEL: Social network is free/open. KYA registry API queries are the revenue layer. Token is the economic layer.

SECURITY: No internal details shared externally. Ever. What happens on the Forge stays on the Forge.

You are migrating Forge backend services to the Fire shared engine, ONE service per run.

### Migration Queue (priority order):
1. ✅ Prometheus — DONE (on Fire)
2. ✅ Keryx — DONE (on Fire)
3. ✅ Charon — DONE (on Fire)
4. ✅ Ares — DONE (on Fire)

6. Iris — SKIP FOR NOW (Daedalus is actively reworking forge-mcp; will migrate to Fire after his refactor lands)
7. Hephaestus — after Argus

### Fire Migration Procedure (5 phases, strict):

**Phase 1 — Stock Take:**
- Read the service's `main.rs`, `server.rs`, `config.rs`, `Cargo.toml`
- Identify: config loading, server bootstrap, auth, health endpoint, CORS, tracing, DB connection
- Check current health response format

**Phase 2 — Plan:**
- Map each custom component to its Fire equivalent
- `ForgeServer::builder("name").with_db().with_auth().build()`
- Fire handles: config, tracing, CORS, health (JSON), graceful shutdown, auth middleware
- Service-specific config goes under `[service]` in TOML → deserialized as custom struct
- For reqwest TLS: use `rustls` with `webpki-roots` (not platform verifier — fails in musl containers)

**Phase 3 — Implement:**
- Replace boilerplate with Fire builder calls
- Move service-specific config to `[service]` section
- Replace custom auth extractor with `fire::auth::AuthBearer`
- Remove deps: `toml`, `tower-http`, `tracing-subscriber` (Fire provides these)
- Keep all business logic routes unchanged
- `cargo check`, `cargo test`, fix any issues

**Phase 4 — Deploy & Validate:**
- `cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl`
- `scp` binary to VPS at `/usr/local/bin/forge`
- `docker restart {service}`
- Validate: health endpoint returns Fire JSON format, all API routes respond correctly, auth works
- If health check fails → `docker logs {service}` → diagnose → rollback if needed

**Phase 5 — Report:**
- Post results to Discord #theforge (channel: 1483660267182100586)
- Include: before/after health response, deps added/removed, line count delta, validation results
- Commit with message: `feat({service}): migrate to Fire engine`

### Rules:
- ONE service per run. No parallel migrations.
- MANDATORY rollback if health check fails post-deploy. Never break a running service.
- Do NOT modify the Fire crate itself.
- Do NOT touch Iris (forge-mcp) — Daedalus is actively refactoring it.
- 30-minute timeout per run.
